articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
articles.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
articles.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

articles.summary_zh: 伊恩· H ·穆雷（ Iain H. Murray ）的《艾米·卡迈克尔：灰烬之美》（ Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes ）是对爱尔兰传教士前往印度的非凡生活的简短复述。接下来是该标题的第4章， “艰难的日子和黄金岁月。“如果说艾米·卡迈克尔的生活有任何模式的话，那就是令人耳目一新的时代，然后是考验的时代，令人兴奋的‘攀登’的时代[…]艾米·卡迈克尔的帖子：令人耳目一新的时代和考验的时代首先出现在真理美国的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 艾米·卡迈克尔：令人耳目一新的时代和审判的时代
articles.content: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ then of walking in dark ravines. In part her explanation was that demonic activity follows the work of the Holy Spirit. As she quoted from George Bowen, When Christianity assumes an aggressive attitude the first result is a great exhibition of Satanic power. Satan’s power to be manifested must be assaulted. 1 Such an understanding does not come so readily to us who do not live, as she did, within sight of demon possession, or within hearing of tom-tom drums calling devotees to idols. Shortly before Walker 2 had left on his last mission, he had been sitting with Amy and others in deck chairs under the stars. ‘We had been talking’, she later wrote, of work and workers, and of those (to me) most wonderful women, who seemed perfectly self-reliant, needing no strong arm alongside. I remember how, suddenly startled at the bare thought of working alone, in the sense of all the burden of responsibility, I exclaimed that I never could do it. Mr Walker laughed. ‘Well, you don’t have to’, he said. 3 Amy was the weaker when her ‘strong arm’ died at the age of fifty-four. What she owed to Walker’s ‘courageous championship’ of the children’s work, ‘through its first very difficult years, no words can tell, nor can words tell how he is missed’. 4 At times, as she faced her loss, she would need to say to herself, ‘Don’t give up, don’t be afraid: go on.’ Prayer for ‘fortitude’ entered her life. There were unsympathetic neighbours who observed the work at Dohnavur who supposed that Amy would now be more vulnerable. One of these was a lawyer who, soon after Walker’s death, wrote with the demand that current work on the building of a wall around the compoundbe stopped, and that a half-built nursery should be pulled down. They were using ground, he claimed, to which they did not have legal title. ‘He had waited till Mr Walker’s death had left us, as he thought, defenceless, almost desolate, and sure to be easily cowed by threats of court trouble.’ The wall building had been prompted by the passage of a tiger through the compound at night; and the new nursery was necessitated by the growing numbers of children for whom Dohnavur had become home. Amy ignored the letter and heard nothing more of the threat. The Dohnavur family of seventy children and grown-ups in 1906, had doubled itself by this date, and the need of more helpers was pressing. Mrs Catherine Carmichael was never able to return. She died on July 14, 1913. A few weeks earlier a letter from her to Amy began with the words, ‘My own most precious earthly possession’. While Amy did not lament her mother’s death—for no Christian death was to be ‘lamented’—in the days ahead she needed to preach to herself, ‘I must remind myself to live in the joy of those gone, not grovel in the sense of my loss.’ Mrs Carmichael had been a constant supporter and representative for Dohnavur in Britain. She acted as the home secretary to whom gifts could be sent, and helped to make her daughter’s books more widely known. In 1912 those books had been noted by Queen Mary, wife of King George V, who expressed her thanks for them. While Amy was busy in 1913 writing Walker of Tinnevelly , there came the possibility of the loss of her closest female friend and helper, Ponnammal, who had been with her ever since, as a young widow, she had come to new life through Walker’s preaching. She now needed surgery for cancer and Amy went with her to a Salvation Army Hospital at Neyyoor for a period. In their absence from Dohnavur (forty-six miles away), and the absence of Mabel Wade who was on furlough, 70 of the children were ill. The need for more medical facilities at Dohnavur itself was evident. After much s
articles.content_zh: 伊恩·H·默里所著的"艾米·卡迈克尔:爱希斯的美人"(Amy Carmichael: Beautiful for Ashes)是爱尔兰传教士到印度的出众生的短篇回忆. 下面是该标题的第4章: " 艰难的日子和黄金年 " 。 如果Amy Carmichael的生活有任何规律的话, 她的部分解释是,妖魔活动遵循了圣灵的工作. 正如她从乔治·博文所引述的那样,当基督教采取侵略态度时,第一个结果就是撒旦力量的伟大展览. 必须攻击撒旦的力量。 1 对我们来说,这种理解并不像她那样活在恶魔拥有的目光下,或者在听到汤姆·通鼓呼唤献给偶像的人面前。 在行走者2号执行上个任务前不久,他一直和艾米等人坐在星空下的甲板椅上. 她后来写道:‘我们谈过了',内容是工作和工人,以及那些似乎完全自力更生、不需要任何坚强的手臂的妇女。 我记得,我突然对独自工作的赤裸裸的想法感到惊奇,因为我肩负着所有的责任,我感到惊叹,我永远做不到。 华克先生笑了 他说,你不必这么做。 3 Amy在54岁时死亡, 她对沃克的“勇敢的冠军”儿童工作所负的责任是,“在第一个非常困难的岁月里,言语无法分辨,言语也无法分辨他是如何被错过的”。 页:1 有时,当她面临损失时,她需要对自己说: " 不要放弃,不要害怕:继续吧。 " 祈求`宽恕'进入她的生活。 有不同情的邻居在多赫纳武尔观察作品,他们认为艾米现在会更加脆弱. 其中一个是一位律师,他在Walker死后不久写道,他要求停止目前在大院周围建造一堵墙的工作,应当拆除一个半建的托儿所。 他声称,他们使用了他们没有合法所有权的地盘。 他一直等待着沃克先生的死像他所想的那样离开我们,他手无寸铁,几乎是荒凉的,而且肯定很容易被法庭麻烦的威胁吓倒了。 墙上建筑的动因是一只老虎在夜间穿过大院;新的托儿所是因越来越多的儿童成为家而必需的。 艾米无视信件,没有听到更多的威胁. 1906年有70个孩子和成年人的多赫纳武尔家族,到这时已使自己翻了一番,迫切需要更多的帮助. 凯瑟琳·卡迈克尔夫人一直没能回来 她于1913年7月14日去世. 几周前,她给艾米的一封信开头写道,“我拥有自己最珍贵的地产”。 Amy没有为她母亲的死感到悲哀——因为没有一个基督徒的死是`在她需要为自己传道的几天里感到悲伤',`我必须提醒自己生活在那些死去的人的欢快中,而不是在我失去的意义上的忧郁'。 卡迈克尔夫人一直是英国多赫纳武尔的支持者和代表。 她担任家庭秘书,可以向她寄送礼物,并帮助使她女儿的书更广为人知。 1912年,这些书被乔治五世国王的妻子玛丽王后所注意到,玛丽王后对之表示感谢. 在1913年艾米忙于写作"Tinnevelly"的Walker(Walker of Tinnevelly)时,出现了失去她最亲密的女性朋友和助手Ponnammal(Ponnammal)的可能性,她从那时起就一直与她在一起,作为一个年轻的寡妇,她通过Walker的传道而来到了新的生活. 她现在需要手术治疗癌症,艾米和她一起去内约尔的救世军医院住了一段时间. 在他们离开多克纳武尔(相距四十六里外),而当时在放假的马贝尔·韦德(英语:Mabel Wade (film))不在的情况下,70个孩子生病了. Dohnavur本身显然需要更多的医疗设施。 这么多之后

articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第二个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。原则2 ：基督徒的生活无法摆脱紧张和冲突。我并不是说基督徒的生活就是这样[…]在基督徒的生活中，《没有逃脱的张力》这篇文章最初出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有摆脱紧张的途径
articles.content: The second of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. Principle 2: There is no escape from tension and conflict in living the Christian life. I do not say that the Christian life is all tension and all conflict. The kind of teaching I am attempting to expose as fallacious is as follows: At a conference a speaker takes a text out of context to which he attaches or from which he extracts a shibboleth – perhaps the shibboleth of Christ living his life through us, or the saving life of Christ, or the abiding life. Then the preacher, having expounded his theory of the Christian life, gives an appeal like this: ‘Child of God, are you weary of the tension of wrestling with your remaining sin? Are you tired of struggling in prayer? Are you weary of having to battle with impure thoughts and thoughts of envy and pride and jealousy? Are you tired of this incessant conflict?’ And every true Christian sits there with his fangs dripping, saying, ‘Oh God, you know I am tired, I would give anything to have one day, one day in which I did not have to battle with dullness of heart and distraction of mind and the seductions to sin that come from without and from within’. And the speaker then says ‘Ah, if you are tired of the tension, weary of the conflict, if you will but take these steps, then Christ will so live his life through you that it will be a life marked by the negation of tension and conflict. You will be so filled with the Spirit, so taken up in the Spirit, that tension and conflict for all intents and purposes will be a thing of the past as long as you maintain the posture of the abiding life. The moment you feel tension and conflict, it is because you slipped out of that life, back to your old ways.’ Now that is not a caricature, that is spelled out in page after page, book after book. Beware of the writings of Watchman Nee! Beware of some of the writings of such as Norman Grubb and Hannah Whithall Smith. Beware of these writings, because if you take them seriously they could drive you either into a world of unreality or into a world of scepticism. Now what proof do I offer from the word of God for that proposition? 1. Because of the reality of indwelling sin with its incessant and powerful actions upon us. Galatians 5:17: ‘The flesh is lusting against the Spirit and the Spirit against the flesh and these two are contrary the one to the other, so that you may not do the things that you would’. And Paul does not go on to say that there is a way to be utterly, totally delivered from that conscious­ness of tension and conflict. He does tell us that we need not be dominated by the flesh: ‘Walk in the Spirit and you shall not fulfil the lusts of the flesh’. But he nowhere says that the consciousness of the flesh’s lusting will be negated, and where flesh is lusting against Spirit, there is conflict. I hold to the time-proven exegesis of Romans 7:14 I do not say that the Christian life is all tension and all conflict. The kind of teaching I am attempting to expose as fallacious is as follows: At a conference a speaker takes a text out of context to which he attaches or from which he extracts a shibboleth – perhaps the shibboleth of Christ living his life through us, or the saving life of Christ, or the abiding life. Then the preacher, having expounded his theory of the Christian life, gives an appeal like this: ‘Child of God, are you weary of the tension of wrestling with your remaining sin? Are you tired of struggling in prayer? Are you weary of having to battle with impure thoughts and thoughts of envy and pride and jealousy? Are you tired of this incessant conflict?’ And every true Christian sits there with his fangs dripping, saying, ‘Oh God, you know I am tired, I would give anything to have one day, one day in which I did not have to battle with dullness of heart and distraction of mind and the seduction

articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有“万能钥匙”
articles.content: The first of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. A question of major importance is ‘How am I to live as a Christian’? It is one thing to be certain on biblical grounds that I have life from Christ, now I must be clear as to how I am to live the life of Christ. My purpose in setting before you some of the major principles of living the Christian life is three-fold: —I wish to sketch in a biblical theology of the Christian life. My purpose is unashamedly one of indoctrination. I wish by God’s help, by Spirit and word, to indoctrinate you in a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. —I wish to inoculate you and to immunize you against the major false views of the Christian life. Some of us desperately wish we had received such an inoculation early in our Christian experience. We spent many years chasing rabbits that we could never catch. We went after experiences and states of mind and heart in the hope that somehow in so doing we would find what it really meant to live as a Christian. —I wish to purge you of any existing misconceptions which you may presently have. It may not be pleasant but it is in your own best interests. We now examine these major principles of the Christian life. Principle 1: There is No One ‘Master Key’ to Living the Christian Life The kind of teaching I am purposing to focus upon in this principle goes something like this: There is a Christian who for many years has found himself in the doldrums. He has had his sails hoisted but he goes nowhere. It seems that he knows little of the wind of the Spirit filling his sails and carrying him anywhere. Or, to change the analogy, he may have his sails hoisted but they seem for ever to be full of holes, and while all around him have hoisted sails and appear to be making progress he seems to be going nowhere. And then one day at a conference or while reading a book or in his own devotions he comes across a passage of Scripture, say John chapter 15, and there he reads in the words of our Lord Jesus that beautiful analogy of the Christian’s relationship to Christ as the relationship of a branch to a vine. This so ignites his own spiritual life that he is almost overnight lifted to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality. Either the holes in his sails get mended or it is as though a mighty zephyr from God himself fills his sails, causing them to billow out to the full. He makes more substantial progress in the Christian life in six months than he has made in the previous six years. This man says that the master key to the Christian life is understanding John 15 and if others will only come to understand the concept of Christ’s relationship to his people as the branch and the vine are related they too will come to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality and reality in their Christian walk. Another example could be someone who has been struggling with a certain besetting sin which leaves him continually bowed down and crippled with guilt. Here is a young Christian struggling with a certain area of besetting sin, unknown to others, and he is constantly bogged down. His wheels are up to the hub-caps in mud, and no matter how much he changes the gears and pushes down on the accelerator he is spinning his wheels and all he is doing is using up petrol and making a mess. He is in that position for weeks and months perhaps, and then one day at a conference or reading a book or in his own devotions he comes to Romans, chapter 6, and he reads the glorious truth that in union with Jesus Christ all that he was as old man has been put to death, and in union with Jesus Christ the totality of the old life has been buried in Christ’s tomb and he is now a new man in Jesus Christ and he sees that he is called upon to reckon it so, and in the light of that, present himself as alive from the dead. articles.content: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books about the Old Testament, Proverbs, faithful presence, the life and influence of Tim Keller, and a whole lot more. Westminster Books is continuing their Reformation sale by offering discounts on ESV Bibles as well as the tremendous new 500th anniversary edition of Tyndale’s New Testament. Recommended Reading How the Mainstream Recruits for the Manosphere. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? Was it because of the closure of traditional mental hospitals, like those of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest ? Was it because of the internet-driven phenomenon of self-diagnosis by very functional influencers? The marginalization of psychiatry as a profession? Or denial, romanticization, and politics?” It Can Happen Here, Too. “As numerous countries in Europe experience riots, many in America are asking, ‘What on earth is happening on the continent that was, in many ways, the cradle of Western civilization?’ As historic buildings, places of worship, and commercial properties combust before our eyes on the nightly news, how are we to make sense of this?” Carl Trueman warns that what’s happening in Europe could also happen in the United States. 8 Ways to Help Your Kids Love the Church. Shiphrah Lakka offers a series of ways to help your kids learn to love the church. “While discipleship at home is extremely important and something every Christian parent should pursue, it can never replace the church. Reading Scripture together, praying as a family, and teaching our children about God within our homes are vital practices. Yet God’s design for believers extends beyond the walls of our homes. He calls us to belong to a community of believers who worship, serve, and do life together.” I Hate Your Halloween Decorations. Marc Sims writes about the reality of Halloween today. “The next time I am out, we will really slow down to take in the diorama you set up of black hooded figures encircling a pentagram-alter with a fake infant set in the middle of it, that way he can become familiar with Satanic rituals and child sacrifice. I mean, where else is he going to get this important cultural experience? Apparently, you are under the impression that becoming desensitized to violence and death is an important step for our whole neighborhood to take in—to celebrate, even. Here, frumpy old Marc ( boooo! ) was worried about why our culture seems ever more eager to relish death and the demonic—but you have shown me that this is really just fun! Save a fake a corpse for me!” Why Paper Books Endure. Daniel Darling explains his ongoing love for paper books (even while he’s not entirely opposed to electronic ones). “When I began my writing career in the early 2,000s, every single writing conference I attended featured speakers who issued grave warnings. E-books would eventually take over. Paper books would be a thing of the past. Libraries are nice relics of another era. Except that didn’t happen.” Something Worth Doing These words by Maltbie Davenport Babcock have often been a challenge to me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if they challenge you as well. articles.title: Is It a Sin to Use AI Porn?
articles.summary: What happens when the people in porn are not real exist, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create ethical pornography that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with real pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn? articles.content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. It is to make something other than God necessary for your joy—in this case, the sexual release that would come with looking at an
articles.content_zh: 在过去20年里,我写了很多关于色情的内容。 在许多不同的时刻,我以许多不同的形式敦促人们考虑一长串反对它的论点。 我很感激与许多人互动, 一些强烈而最有效的反对使用色情作品的论据是基于参与其中的人的人道. 因此,例如,在“停止看色情电影的7个好理由”中,我写道,我们需要考虑制作者的成本。 " 色情制品的制作者付出了高昂的代价 -- -- 他们的身体、灵魂、精神健康、尊严、未来的代价。 你所欣赏的大量色情作品都是由人们违背自己的意愿所创造的. 简单的事实是,通过看色情片, 你正在看强奸,并从中获得乐趣。 你成为性暴力的自愿参与者,你允许屏幕上那个演员为取悦而受苦。” 即使有些色情作品是合意的,但大量的色情作品却不是,观众也无法知道哪个是. 同样,在“每当你看到色情制品时,你就会犯下八起罪行”中,我说,观看色情制品的人犯有性侵犯罪。 “为一帮银行劫匪驾驶逃跑的汽车的人,将因犯下这种罪行而被杀害的人受到谋杀的指控。 自愿观看性攻击以达到抚慰目的的人理应犯有性攻击罪。 而令人恶心的色情作品数量在性质上是暴力的,展现出男性利用女性. 有时,这些妇女自愿从事这种有辱人格的工作,有时她们被迫或被强奸。 目睹这种令人发指的一团糟,就是参与其中,并承担其中的道德污点。” 虽然这些与反对色情制品的唯一论点相去甚远, 但是当参与色情的人物不再是人时会怎样呢? 当它们不再存在,而只是由AI产生时会发生什么? 大赦国际能否允许我们制造出“道德色情制品”,解决与“真正的”色情制品有关的最主要关切之一? 换句话说,看AI生成的色情片是不是罪过? (为了我们的目的,我们将假定,我们已经在拒绝利用像现有个人那样的深层假色情,认为这种色情在道德上是令人厌恶的,既不道德又非法。) 相反,我们正在考虑完全由大赦国际创造的人的形象。 ) 简单的回答是:看AI生成的色情片和看人造色情片一样罪恶. 虽然有些论点可能并不那么相关,但大多数论点没有改变。 在我解释方式和原因之前,我要你们聆听一个警告:我们都是通过遵守严格的法律条文来规避法律精神的专家。 我们内心深处有些东西想藐视赋予我们的规则,我们变得有技巧为我们这样做的方式辩护。 这往往涉及将道德降低为严格的二进制,然后说服自己,因为我们没有公然违法,我们遵守了法律。 这恰恰是耶稣时代的法利赛人的罪过,他们严格地说要将自己在花园所种的调味品的两倍之多,但却未能按照正义、慈悲和忠诚的更高原则活下来。 我们每个人都有法利赛人 考虑到这一点,以下是使用大赦国际制作的色情制品的罪责。 你仍然在贪欲, 即使你在贪欲 一个人只存在于屏幕上。 性欲是渴望非法的性快感,而渴望非法的性快感是寻求上帝所禁止的满足. 是为了让上帝之外的东西成为你欢乐的必备之物——在这种情况下,是性释放,而这种性释放会伴随着对一个...

articles.content: Good morning. May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of good books from New Growth Press and other publishers. Among them you’ll find several good options from Jared Wilson. Recommended Reading Goodbye, ‘Sam’s Club’ Megachurch. Hello, Stained Glass. Christianity Today reports on what I consider a welcome trend: church buildings that look like churches instead of warehouses. It begins this way: “Trinity Presbyterian finally has a church building of its own. That building has arches. And carved hammerbeams that tell the story of the Bible.” 3 Reasons Why Christians Should Lay “R.I.P.” to Rest. Nick Batzig thinks it would be best for Christians to lay R.I.P. to rest. “I’ve noticed something of a concerning trend over the past several years. It is the way in which believers speak about culture-impacting individuals at their deaths. Instead of simply expressing appreciation for their life and achievements, it has become commonplace for Christians to use the shorthand ‘R.I.P.’ (rest in peace) on social media when speaking of individuals in whose lives there was no evidence of saving grace at their death. At the risk of sounding ill-tempered, I wish to set out several reasons why I am troubled by this occurrence.” Go Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. Looking to put down roots in God’s Word? The Grow app from Ligonier Ministries gives you clear Bible teaching and guides your daily study for a deeper walk with Christ. Ministry Partners can also access the verse-by-verse notes from the Reformation Study Bible directly in the app and get reliable answers to their theological questions with the Ask Ligonier intelligent assistant. Not a Ligonier Ministry Partner yet? Try these features for 30 days when you download Grow and sign in. (Sponsored) Beauty Demands to Be Noticed. Michael Jensen is right: beauty demands to be noticed. He tells about people who understand the connection between beauty and transcendence and says, “Clearly, the reductive and polemical explanation of the atheists isn’t proving to be compelling. People can’t square their deeply felt experience of the world with that. To the people I’ve been speaking with, at least, the world simply cannot be reduced to its material components, nor can its coherence be explained by resorting to chance.” Aslan Sane: The Bowiefication of Narnia. I’ve got a pair of articles to share that comment on the forthcoming Narnia movies, each taking a different perspective. In the first, the writer remembers the old Narnia series from her childhood and bridges from there to what we know of the new one. She’s not impressed with it. Aslan and the Christians Who Can’t Be Enchanted. In the second, the author rebukes people like me (and the previous author) who have expressed concerns. He reminds us that it’s a movie for kids and that we don’t really know much about it yet. (I’d say he writes with some degree of exaggeration when he accuses me of losing my mind, but I’m glad to consider what he says nonetheless.) The Day of Pioneer Missions Is Not Over. Writing for Desiring God, my friend Tim Keesee wants us to know that the day of pioneer missions is not over. “Pioneer missionaries are still needed today because there are vast territories and high-rise megacities where the gospel message has yet to reach.” Videos Worth Watching Here are several brief videos that are worth your time. 5 Signs Your Church Might Be Too Seeker Sensitive. Adriel Sanchez explains seeker sensitivity and offers signs your church might lean too much in that direction and become seeker driven. How to Leave a Church Well. Hershael York speaks specifically to pastors to explain how and when to leave a church well. The Enduring Word. This short film from Crossway celebrates God’s providence through the history of Bible translation. Flashback What’s The Point Of Family Devotions? articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. (This is a new feature I trialed last week. The response was positive, so I’m going to keep it going. I have tried to improve the format and layout to make it easier to read.) Books for Everyone Crossway The Westminster Confession of Faith A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith Endorsed by: Joel R. Beeke, Michael Horton, Keith A. Mathison, Robert Letham, and Jonathan L. Master Publisher’s description What is Reformed theology? In 1646, a group of theologians composed what is arguably the most comprehensive statement of faith, the Westminster Confession. Their efforts to preserve Protestant theology against opposing beliefs endured. Today, amid growing interest in Reformed Christianity, the Westminster Confession remains an indispensable guide for living out doctrine, worship, and church governance sola Scriptura, “by Scripture alone.” This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies. Clear, thorough explanations of principles, including the Trinity, creation, providence, baptism, last judgment, and more, make this the definitive guide on Reformed Christian doctrine. The essays are written by faculty from Reformed Theological Seminary in their areas of expertise, ensuring a trustworthy and high-quality text for church leaders, teachers and students of theology, and laypeople. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway I Don’t Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist Updated Edition Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek Endorsed by: Gavin Ortlund, Sean McDowell, Gregory Koukl, Alisa Childers, and Josh Howerton Publisher’s description To some, the concept of having faith in a higher power or a set of religious beliefs is nonsensical. Indeed, many view religion in general, and Christianity in particular, as unfounded and unreasonable. Frank Turek and Norman Geisler argue, however, that Christianity is not only more reasonable than all other belief systems but is indeed more rational than unbelief itself. With conviction and clear thinking, Turek and Geisler guide readers through some of the traditional, tested arguments for the existence of a creator God. They move into an examination of the source of morality and the reliability of the New Testament accounts concerning Jesus. The final section of the book deals with a detailed investigation of the claims of Christ. This updated volume with fresh arguments will be an interesting read for those skeptical about Christianity, as well as a helpful resource for Christians seeking to articulate a more sophisticated defense of their faith. Buy it at Amazon . Baker Books Giver of All Good God as the Beginning and End of Ethics Chase R. Kuhn Publisher’s description Where do our ethics come from? Are they based on unchanging realities or subject to revision as human culture develops and changes? What distinguishes Christian ethics from other moral claims? And how can Christians engage these questions with clarity and confidence—without either abandoning their convictions or abandoning the conversation? In Giver of All Good , Chase R. Kuhn argues that the answer begins not with ourselves—our feelings, our culture, our moral intuitions—but with God. What we believe about God shapes how we live. Our theology guides
articles.content_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的一天,所以每周我都会告诉你,我最密切地关注的出版商刚刚给我们带来了什么。 本周来自整群改革派学者对"威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)提出了实质性的新评论,并更新了一出名作"通俗小说"(Apologetics Book),一出给孩子们的几本书和一出"ESV"的新版本. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 (这是上星期我试演的新节目) 回应是积极的, 我努力改进格式和布局,使其更容易阅读。 ) 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑, 乔尔·R·比克、Michael Horton、Keith A. Mathison、Robert Letham和Jonathan L. Master Publishers对改革神学的描述。 1646年,一群神学家组成了可以说是最全面的信仰声明"威斯敏斯特忏悔". 他们努力保护新教神学,反对对立的信仰。 如今,在对改革后的基督教越来越感兴趣的情况下,威斯敏斯特忏悔仍然是“仅靠圣经”活出学说、崇拜和教会治理的不可或缺的指南。 这份重要的散文集为21世纪的读者提供了威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔的可获取指南. 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其应用以及任何争议。 对原则,包括"三一","创造","天赐","受洗","最后的判断"等进行明确,彻底的解释,使这成为"改革后基督教学说"的决定性指南. 论文由改革神学院的教师在其专业领域撰写,确保教会领导人、神学教师和学生以及外行者能够获得可靠和高质量的文本。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway I don't have enough Faith to be an Atheist 更新版 Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek 由加文·奥尔特伦德,肖恩·麦克道威尔,格雷戈里·库克尔,艾莉莎·柴尔德斯和乔什·豪尔顿出版商的描述认可 对一些人来说,对更高权力或一套宗教信仰有信仰的概念是没有意识的. 事实上,许多人认为,一般宗教,特别是基督教,是毫无根据和不合理的。 然而,弗兰克·图雷克和诺曼·盖斯勒(Norman Geisler)认为,基督教不仅比所有其他信仰体系更合理,而且确实比不信本身更合理. 以信念和清晰的思考,图雷克和盖斯勒指导读者通过一些传统的,经过考验的关于创造出神存在的论点. 他们开始研究道德渊源和"新约"中有关耶稣的叙述的可靠性. 该书的最后一节详细论述对基督的主张的调查. 这本附有新论点的增订本,对于那些对基督教持怀疑态度的人来说,将是一个有趣的读物,也是基督教徒寻求更尖端地捍卫其信仰的有用资源。 在亚马逊买的 Baker Books of All Good God的出品人作为伦理学的开始和结束 Chase R. Kuhn出版社的描述 我们的道德从何而来? 它们是建立在不断变化的现实基础上,还是随着人类文化的发展和变化而需要加以修改? 基督教道德与其他道德主张有什么区别? 基督徒如何以明确和自信的方式处理这些问题,而不放弃他们的信念或放弃对话? Chase R. Kuhn指出,答案不是从我们自己开始的——我们的感情、我们的文化和我们的道德直觉——而是从上帝开始的。 我们对上帝的信仰 塑造了我们的生活 我们的神学指南

articles.content: Good morning from somewhere in rural Colorado. I’m here for the next few days for meetings and training, as well as a bit of hiking and photography and, best of all, some quiet times of writing. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include O. Palmer Robertson’s two-part Christ of the Consummation , which was commended by, among others, D.A. Carson, Sinclair Ferguson, and Joel Beeke. You’ll also find lots of great deals from Zondervan from books that are related to Protestant theology. Recommended Reading Can a Christian Be Demon-Possessed? I know there are many people who are concerned that, even though they are Christians, they may still be possessed by demons. Anthony Faggiano explains why that is not a legitimate fear. “Desire entices us; yielding gives birth to sin; sin grows toward death. Satan can tempt us, but we remain responsible for our desires and decisions. We cannot blame an indwelling demon for what Scripture traces to our sinful hearts. Yet God hasn’t left believers powerless. Through his Holy Spirit, we can begin to put sin to death and walk in obedience.” 7 Keys for Thriving in Lifelong Ministry. I enjoyed reading Joel Beeke’s keys for thriving in pastoral ministry. “Looking back over my ministry over the long term is much more encouraging than looking at it in the short term. A long-term perspective helps me see those who have been saved by the Spirit through my sermons, those marriages that have been strengthened, and even the fruitfulness of elders and deacons who were unsaved when I arrived at my church 40 years ago but have since come to know the Lord personally, vibrantly, and experientially.” Why Does Everyone Else’s Life Seem Better Than Mine? There are some good insights in Zachary Conover’s article on comparison and envy. “Comparison has a way of making us dissatisfied with things we once received with gratitude. We can be thankful for our homes, our families, our work, and the opportunities God has given us. But then we see someone else’s life. We scroll through reel after reel, and suddenly our own begins to feel inadequate. Their opportunities seem greater. Their accomplishments seem more significant. Their circumstances seem more desirable. Am I the only one who doesn’t have it all together? Why don’t I have what they have? And without realizing it, we begin to measure the goodness of God toward us against what He has given to someone else.” Put the Destination in the Frame. John Seel has a guest piece on Aaron Renn’s Substack that offers some helpful points on the way we talk about young men. “We are talking about men incorrectly. We frame discussions of men in terms of problems – the ‘crisis of boys and men’ or ‘failure to launch’ – rather than the destination we want men to arrive at. If we want a different outcome, we need to change the frame of our discussions about men to center on the new reality we want to create. We need a frame that naturally leads us to answer the key question: What kind of men do we want our boys to become?” Welcome to the Valley of Pain. This article from The Atlantic points out, correctly, that the “safe internet” is shrinking and that we need to be more vigilant than ever. “For the next year or two, if not longer, the internet is going to feel a bit touch and go, and more dangerous than we’ve come to expect. ‘It’s going to feel like the sky is falling’ for a while, Prince said. There’s a decades-long backlog of bugs in software written without much review or scrutiny—which was more or less fine so long as there was a very small number of skilled hackers. Over the past two decades, companies, governments, and individuals have been lulled into a false sense of security: Most people don’t think twice about punching credit-card numbers into the website of a local restaurant or gift shop, or forking over a home address and phone number in just about any customer survey. But the internet was always a dangerous place. We’re just waking up from a trance.” Adoption Is Not a T

articles.title_zh: 在婚姻中培养亲密感
articles.content: I recently spent a couple of weeks preparing a great deal of fresh material for a weekend-long marriage seminar. Along the way, I often found myself convicted by the content I was preparing. As I readied myself to teach others, I had to consider the ways in which I needed to be a student before I should be a teacher. One area this proved true was intimacy in marriage—but a kind of intimacy I think many of us seldom consider. There is no doubt that marriage is meant to involve a husband and wife baring their bodies before one another, so that marriage is the context in which a man and woman can experience what it is to be naked and unashamed—to be fully bared, yet fully accepted. And because marriage is meant to be the deepest kind of unity two human beings can experience, it makes sense that there is a physical component to it through which two bodies are literally joined together. This is usually what we mean when we discuss intimacy in marriage. It is my understanding that this kind of intimacy, while real, is also in a way representative or symbolic. It is a demonstration of a unity between two people that is not merely body-deep , but fully soul-deep. Physical intimacy is both significant and essential to marriage, but it is not meant to be the sum total of the intimacy shared between a husband and wife. Yet as Aileen and I have interacted with other couples, we have observed that many husbands and wives find it easier to bare their bodies than their souls. Even as they routinely give themselves to one another physically, they can withhold a great deal relationally and emotionally. Even as they give themselves in free and joyful lovemaking, they can stop short of a greater baring, which is the baring of their souls and the revealing of the deep recesses of their hearts. As Aileen and I discussed this together, we had to conclude that this is something we are prone to as well. It’s not that we hold back shocking secrets or scandalous sins that would cause the other to recoil in dismay or disgust. It’s that we are both reserved people who find it hard to let another person in. We are both wounded people who have been hurt by those who have misused information we have revealed to them. And then I suppose we are both prideful or distrustful people who hold back the pieces of ourselves that we think might cause the other person to lower their respect for us. But by holding back, we are failing to live with full transparency and, therefore, failing to live with full intimacy. The baring of our bodies exceeds the baring of our souls. There is an irony to this, because I am convinced there is a deep longing within each of us to be known. We want someone else to know us as we truly are and to still love us and give us their approval. But even while we want it on one level, we resist it on another, because we wonder what that other person will think of us if they know our deep thoughts, our secret longings, and our hidden fears. We wonder if they will still respect us if they know what causes us to feel shame or express remorse. Perhaps we doubt they’ll still love us if they know who we are far beneath the surface. Still, there is this longing to be known, to be as bare emotionally as we can be physically—and still to be loved and accepted. It is this longing that we never address when we hold back from revealing who and what we truly are, when we refuse to foster a deep soul intimacy—an intimacy that is then represented by, rather than superseded by, sexual intimacy. So how can we foster this kind of baring? By letting our spouse really know us, which may mean creating times and contexts for lengthy, deep, and uninterrupted conversation. This will involve asking good questions and then listening attentively so we can come to a correct rather than trite or hasty understanding of what is being communicated. To really know and be known is the work of a lifetime. It is work, but work worth committing to. By assuring one another that no
articles.content_zh: 我最近花了几周时间 准备了大量的新材料 为周末的婚姻研讨会。 一路走来,我常常发现自己被我准备的内容定罪. 当我准备去教别人时,我不得不在做教师之前考虑我需要成为学生的方式。 婚姻中的亲密关系是事实, 毫无疑问,婚姻意味着丈夫和妻子在彼此面前禁止其身体,因此,婚姻是男女能够体验裸体和无羞无耻——被完全禁止,但却被完全接受的背景。 因为婚姻是两个人类能够经历的最深层次的团结,所以它有一个物理成分,通过它,两个身体可以真正结合在一起。 这通常是我们讨论婚姻亲密关系时的意思. 我的理解是,这种亲密关系虽然是真实的,但在某种程度上也是有代表性的或象征性的。 它表明两个人之间的团结 不仅仅是身体深处,而且是灵魂深处 肉体亲密关系对婚姻既重要又重要,但并非夫妻共有亲密关系的总和。 然而,随着艾琳和我与其他夫妇的互动,我们观察到,许多丈夫和妻子发现露出自己的身体比灵魂更容易. 即使在他们习惯上互相施舍的时候,他们也可以在感情上和感情上保持相当的克制。 即使在他们自由而欢快地做爱时,他们也可以停止更大的禁酒,这就是他们的灵魂被束缚,以及他们内心深处的沉睡。 正如我和艾琳一起讨论的那样,我们不得不得出结论,这也是我们容易看到的。 并不是我们隐瞒令人震惊的秘密或可耻的罪恶, 我们都是有保留的人, 我们都是被滥用我们所透露的信息的人所伤害的受伤者。 然后我想,我们都是骄傲或不信任的人,他们屏蔽着我们自己的碎片,我们认为这可能会使他人降低对我们的尊重. 但是,通过阻挠,我们没有完全透明地生活,因此,没有完全亲密地生活。 身体的阻断 超过了灵魂的阻断 这一点具有讽刺意味,因为我相信,我们每个人都有很深的渴望要知道。 我们希望其他人了解我们的真实身份,仍然爱我们,并给予我们批准。 但是,即使我们希望在一个层次上,我们抵制另一个层次,因为我们想知道,如果其他人知道我们的深思熟虑,我们的秘密渴望,以及我们隐藏的恐惧,我们会怎么想。 我们想知道,如果他们知道是什么使我们感到羞愧或表示悔恨,他们是否仍然尊重我们。 也许我们怀疑如果他们知道我们是谁, 然而,人们仍渴望知道这一点,希望我们能像身体上那样裸露出情感——仍然希望得到爱和接受。 正是这种渴望,当我们不愿透露我们真正是谁和什么时,当我们拒绝培养一种深厚的灵魂亲密关系时,我们从未谈到这种渴望——这种亲密关系由性亲密关系而不是取而代之。 那么,我们如何促进这种酒吧? 通过让我们的配偶真正了解我们,这可能意味着为冗长、深入和不间断的对话创造时间和背景。 这将涉及提出好的问题,然后认真倾听,以便我们能够对所传达的内容有一个正确而不是老练或仓促的理解。 真正知道和被了解是一生的工作。 这是工作,但值得致力于工作。 互相保证不会

articles.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals If all goes well, today’s Kindle deals should include several important books that deal with a Christian understanding of science. Westminster Books is offering a deal this week on the two-part John Calvin’s Illustrated Institutes , which drives the price as low as 50% off. Recommended Reading This Is Roman Catholicism. Here’s a tremendous new project from the Reformanda Initiative—a free documentary series that “offers a firsthand look at often-overlooked yet integral aspects of Roman Catholic theology and practice, challenging idealized perceptions of Rome and encouraging informed, biblical discernment—particularly among those drawn to it. This docuseries is made primarily for Protestant Christians who want to understand what Rome teaches and practices. Featuring: Leonardo De Chirico, Mark Dever, Kevin DeYoung, Albert Mohler, Lauren Montenegro, and Michael Reeves.” Three Ways to Walk With Those Who Grieve. Kirsten Black outlines three ways that any of us can walk faithfully and compassionately with those who are in a time of deep grief. “Often, we do not know how to step into spaces of loss. There is a beautiful and godly desire to bring comfort, yet when facing the reality of walking with the grieving, we are also confronted with the limits of the comfort we can actually offer. This holy work often brings with it an acute awareness of how easy it is to say the wrong thing and unintentionally add more pain to the one who is already suffering.” Explore the Reformation in Ligonier’s Grow App . The Protestant Reformation was not a minor theological dispute—it was a recovery of the biblical gospel. With Reformation Day coming this Saturday, you can explore a variety of free Reformation-themed teaching series with R.C. Sproul in the Grow app from Ligonier Ministries. Download the app and study the five solas , the life of Martin Luther, and much more. (Sponsored) 5 Ways Men Can Serve the Church & 5 Ways Women Can Serve the Church. A pair of articles from Ligonier Ministries offers distinct and meaningful ways that both men and women can serve within the local church. Christian Universalism Is Alive (Just Go to a Funeral). Yes, I have observed as well that funerals are the events where we are most likely to see evidence of Christian universalism. “I’ve been to many funerals and memorial services in my life, and through the years, I’ve encountered religious people who give off the impression that they believe everyone goes to heaven. Culture gives the same impression. Words reveal worldviews. The deceased person may not have received Christ by faith, may not have gone to church, may have even lived an unrepentant and selfish life, and some people still seem to assume they went to a ‘better place’ or went to heaven. Might Christian Universalism be more prevalent than we think?” Stinginess and the Generosity of God. Randy Alcorn contrasts the stinginess of human beings—and even Christian human beings—with the generosity of God. “A life characterized by greed and stinginess is neither Spirit-filled nor Christlike — nor is it happy. If we know Jesus, we will become more and more like our generous God.” Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (And False) Conversions. Writing for 9Marks, John Lee explains how unclear evangelism can lead to false conversions. “When we are unclear about the urgency of conversion, the cost of conversion, or the accountability that should accompany conversion, we risk leaving people deceived about their eternal state. Ultimately, our job is simply to proclaim the gospel clearly, trust God to open people’s hearts to the truth, and provide ongoing discipleship to those who respond in repentance and faith.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. articles.content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 格蕾丝和平安 销售和交易 如果一切顺利,今天的Kindle交易应该包括几本重要书籍,涉及基督教对科学的理解。 威斯敏斯特图书公司本周在约翰·加尔文两地的Illustrated Institutes提供一笔交易, 推荐阅读 这是罗马天主教。 以下是Reformanda倡议的一个巨大的新项目,这是一部免费的纪录片系列,“第一手看一看罗马天主教神学和实践中经常被高瞻远瞩但不可分割的方面,挑战对罗马理想化的看法,并鼓励知情的、圣经上的分辨——特别是在那些被吸引的人中。 这种道克系列主要为新教基督徒所制作,他们想了解罗马的教义和实践. 表演:莱昂纳多·德·奇里科、马克·德维尔、凯文·德杨、阿尔伯特·莫勒、劳伦·黑山和迈克尔·里夫斯。” 柯尔斯滕·布莱克概述了我们中任何人都能与那些处于极度悲痛的时代的人们忠实而富有同情心地行走的三种方式. “当然,我们不知道如何进入损失空间。 有一种美丽而神通地渴望带来舒适,然而当面对与悲伤相伴而行的现实时,我们也面临着我们实际所能提供的舒适的限度. 这种神圣的工作往往使人们敏锐地意识到说错话是多么容易,无意中给已经遭受痛苦的人增加了更多的痛苦。” 探索Ligonier Grow App的改造。 新教改革并不是一个小的神学纠纷——这是圣经福音的收复. 随着本周六的改造日的到来,你可以在利戈尼耶各部的"成长"应用中,与R.C.Sproul一起探索各种自由改造主题的教学系列. 下载应用程序并研究五索拉斯, 马丁路德的生活,还有更多。 (赞助) 5 道:男人可以为教会服务 5道:女人可以为教会服务. 利戈尼耶各部的一对文章提供了独特而有意义的方法,男女都可以在地方教会中服务。 基督教世界主义是活的(去葬礼吧). 是的,我也注意到,葬礼是我们最有可能看到基督教普遍主义证据的事件。 「我一生中参加过许多葬礼和追悼会, 文化也给人同样的印象。 语出出世相. 死者可能没有信仰接受基督,可能没有去教堂,甚至过着不悔改和自私的生活,有些人似乎仍然认为他们去了"更好的地方"或去天堂. 基督教世界主义会比我们想象的更盛行吗? 坚忍与神通相. articles.content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: What a God We Serve! (A Devotional) Ambient Earth Wildlife Photographer of the Year What Animals Can You Outrun? Who Would Have Dreamed 🎵 Bird Radio Who Is Like the Lord? 🎵 1. What a God We Serve! God has wisdom to know what is best and wisdom to know how to accomplish it by the best possible means. He also has power to execute it all. But we may wonder, as it pertains to us, what is his will? What does his wisdom determine is best? What is he accomplishing through the execution of his power? The book of Romans contains words of tremendous comfort: “And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose” (Romans 8:28). God’s will is our good, which means that God’s wisdom and power are directed at accomplishing what is ultimately for our good, and accomplishing it all in the best ways. All the things we experience, all the things we undergo, all the things we endure, all the things we celebrate and lament, the things that make us laugh and cry—all of them are born of God’s love, directed at our good, and executed in a way that is nothing short of perfect. What a God we serve! And what a God we worship today. 2. Ambient Earth Ambient Earth is a great project! A guy named Seán Doran took 49,000 of Butch Wilmore’s photos taken aboard the International Space Station, then repaired, remastered, and retimed them to create an incredible 7.5-hour, 4K journey around the earth. He also added Chris Hadfield’s recording of the sounds of the ISS, which honestly gets a bit annoying, so you may want to mute it and then put on some nice instrumental music in its place. This is a great video to just leave playing on a TV in a public place. (While we’re on the subject of Butch Wilmore, he’s a believer and recently wrote Stuck in Space , which you may enjoy.) 3. Wildlife Photographer of the Year I always enjoy a good photography contest and, for whatever reason, this is the time of the year when many of them announce their winners. That’s the case with the Wildlife Photographer of the Year contest, which had 65,000 entries from 121 countries and territories. That link leads to The Atlantic ‘s gallery of highlights, though if you prefer to see the official site, you can find it here . As you’d expect, many of the photos are nothing short of stunning. 4. What Animals Can You Outrun? I suppose we all wonder at one time or another whether we would be able to outrun certain animals. The BBC did some research to find out which animals we’d possibly be able to outrun and the ones we definitely wouldn’t. Overall, the news isn’t particularly good. It’s a good thing God made us smart, since he didn’t make us particularly fast. See: The animals you can’t outrun – and the ones you can . 5. Who Would Have Dreamed Over a decade ago, Sovereign Grace Music released a Christmas album titled Prepare Him Room . I guess they have dusted off that album and decided to give it new life by recording a live version of it. I’m glad they’ve done so, because it has some really good songs on it. My favorite, and one we sing seasonally at Grace Fellowship Church, is also the first track they’ve re-released: “ Who Would Have Dreamed .” 6. Bird Radio Bird Radio is a neat concept—you simply tune in to hear the calls of different birds from all around the world. God displays his creativity in many different ways and the sheer variety of bird calls is a pretty impressive one. (Also on the subject of birds, did you know the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service maintains a feather atlas so you can learn about the ones you happen to find?) 7. Bonus: Who Is Like the Lord? That well-known and much-loved songwriting combination of Matt/Matt/Keith/Kristyn released a new song this week: “ Who Is Like the Lord? “ Whose wisdom s
articles.content_zh: 在每周的Works & Wonders专栏中,我把简短的奉献与我整个星期所收集的其他有趣而令人振奋的作品结合起来。 希望你们能欣赏这周的作品! 它包括:我们所崇拜的神! 地球野生生物年度摄影师, 谁会梦见"鸟之电台" "谁像上帝"? 上帝有智慧,知道什么是最佳的,有智慧,知道如何用尽可能好的手段完成它. 他也有权力执行这一切。 但是,我们可能会怀疑,它与我们有关,他的意志是什么? 他的智慧决定什么是最好的? 他通过行使权力取得了什么成就? 罗马人书中载有令人极为慰藉的话:“我们知道,对于热爱上帝的人来说,一切事情都为善而工作,对于按照他的目的被召唤的人来说”(罗马人8:28)。 上帝的旨意是我们的好意,这意味着上帝的智慧和力量旨在完成最终为我们造福的事业,并以最好的方式完成这一切. 我们所经历的一切,我们所经历的一切,我们所忍受的一切,我们所庆贺和哀叹的一切,我们所欢笑和哭泣的一切——所有这一切都是由上帝的爱所生出,以我们的利益为目标,并以完全完美的方式被处决. 我们所崇拜的神啊! 今天我们崇拜的神是什么? 2. 地球环境是一个伟大的项目! 一位名叫Seán Doran的人在国际空间站上拍摄了49,000张布奇·威尔莫尔的照片,随后修复,重新制作,并重新定时,创造了令人难以置信的7.5小时4K环绕地球的旅程. 他还加入了克里斯·哈德菲尔德(Chris Hadfield)对国际空间站声音的录制, 老实说,这有点烦人,所以你可能想关掉它,然后用一些很好的器乐代替它。 这是一个伟大的视频 只是离开 在电视播放 在公共场所。 (虽然我们讨论的是Butch Wilmore, 他是一个信徒, 3. (关于鸟类,你是否知道美国鱼类和野生动物服务局维持了羽毛图集,以便你了解你偶然找到的?) 7. 奖金:谁像主? 马特/马特/凯斯/克里斯廷的这首著名和受人喜爱的歌曲的组合本周发行了一首新歌:“谁像主?”

articles.content: Good morning. This Weekend edition of A La Carte has some long-form content, some think pieces, some lists of the most popular articles from the week gone by, and a whole collection of recommendations from readers like you. Enjoy! Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books on sexuality, forgiveness, Habakkuk, Revelation, and more. Recommended Reading Not everyone is familiar with the term concupiscence , but most of us are familiar with some of the debates surrounding it. For example, are our unholy desires sinful, or is it only sinful to act out on those desires? This question often arises when we discuss same-sex attraction. Writing for Logos, Mark Jones explores the concept of concupiscence from a Reformed perspective. In brief, concupiscence (concupiscentia) originates from the Latin verb concupisco, which means ‘to ardently desire.’ There are proper, non-sinful forms of desire, which we would call ‘non-sinful concupiscence.’ For example, Jesus said to his disciples, ‘I have earnestly desired [ἐπεθύμησα] to eat this Passover with you before I suffer’ (Luke 22:15). But because we live in a fallen world, concupiscence typically has in view sinful desire, and usually in reference to sinful sexual desires. Because sin is the privation (lack) of righteousness and proneness to evil, concupiscence involves not just the acts but the desire of the person. Sinful concupiscence can be understood from God’s moral law: ‘You shall not covet’ (Exod 20:17). Concupiscence: Are Our Unholy Desires Sinful? The Guardian tells a strange and twisting tale of a death, a scandal, and a desire for revenge, which it summarizes like this: “After his mother died, Otto became convinced he’d been wronged by the forensic investigators – and that one of them was a fraud. The truth was even stranger.” Here’s how the article begins: On a balmy, quiet evening in June 2020, Otto’s elderly mother, Doria, was fading in her Munich apartment. As she lay with her eyes closed, her pale face, framed by her white hair, was calm. Otto, masked, gloved and draped in a sterile apron, dozed in a chair beside her. Otto, who sometimes goes by the name Rainer, and whose last name is only known as “Z” because of Germany’s strict privacy laws, was a doctor who had cared for his mother for years, ever since she had suffered a stroke and moved in with him. He described the course of that night to me. He woke to the sound of her short breath and tried to sit her upright. Her eyes were shut, and her lips pursed. She stopped breathing. Otto reached for his phone to call for help, but then Doria opened her eyes and stared into his. She smiled, drew one last deep breath, shut her eyes again, and lay still. A Death, a Plagiarism Scandal and a Quest for Revenge: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren sees Beatrix Potter as an example of true conservatism, and explains why that’s the case in a really interesting article about the life of someone whose work we are probably all familiar with. There is a type of academic who can only get noticed by attacking the legacies of greater men and women, and a prime example was cited by Matthew Dennison in The Spectator in his essay “Don’t Cancel Beatrix Potter.” The beloved children’s author has become the target of “specialist in postcolonial literature” Dr. Emily Zobel Marshall, who hilariously claims that Potter failed “to acknowledge her indebtedness to an oral storytelling tradition of enslaved Africans working on American plantations” and that this contributes to “a damaging and recurring appropriation of Black cultural forms that continues today.” This is frivolous stuff, and Marshall’s claims are a parasitic attempt to gain fifteen minutes of fame by slandering a woman who cannot defend herself. Dennison handily rebuts Marshall, and I’m glad he did—but I can’t help but think that fortunately, some writers are uncancellable. Potter’s books have sold 250 million copies. articles.content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 这本周末版的A La Carte 有一些长式内容,一些思想作品,一些周来最受欢迎的文章列表,还有你这样的读者提出的一整套建议. 慢慢来! 今天的销售和交易包括性、宽恕、哈巴克克、启示录等书籍。 建议阅读 并非每个人都熟悉“巧妙”一词, 例如,我们的恶性欲望是有罪的,还是只对这些欲望采取行动是有罪的? 这个问题经常在我们讨论同性吸引力时出现. 为Logos写作,马克·琼斯从改革的视角探索了巧妙的概念. 简而言之,康克塞克语(concupiscentia)起源于拉丁语动词concupisco,意为"强烈的欲望". 我们称之为“无耻的谦虚”。 例如,耶稣对他的门徒说:我的确希望在我受苦之前与你们一起吃这个逾越节。 但是,因为我们生活在一个堕落的世界中,巧妙通常会考虑到罪恶的欲望,通常会提到罪恶的性欲望。 因为罪恶是正义被剥夺(黑暗),容易被邪恶所侵扰,所以巧妙的行为不仅涉及行为,而且涉及人的欲望. 从上帝的道德法则可以理解罪恶的欺骗: " 你不应该贪婪 " (20:17). 混淆:我们的不祥愿望是否有罪? 《卫报》讲述了一个奇怪而曲折的死亡、丑闻和复仇欲望的故事,它这样总结道 : “ 在他母亲死后,奥托开始相信自己被法医调查人员冤枉了 — — 其中一人是骗子。 真相甚至是陌生的。” 以下是文章的开头: 2020年6月,奥托的年长母亲多莉亚正在慕尼黑的公寓中消亡。 当她闭上眼睛躺下时,被她白发所陷的她苍白的脸色是平静的. Otto被蒙上面具 被手套并被涂上不育的围裙 睡在她旁边的椅子上 奥托有时取名"雷纳"(Rainer),由于德国严格的隐私法,他的姓只被称作"Z",自她中风后一直和他一起住入,他是一个照顾他母亲多年的医生. 他向我描述了那晚的经过。 他醒来时听到她短促的呼吸声,想让她坐直. 她的眼睛被闭上了 嘴唇被包住了 她停止了呼吸。 奥托打电话求救,但后来多莉娅睁开眼睛并盯着他. 她微笑了,画了最后一口深呼吸,又闭上了眼睛,躺了下来。 A Death, a Plagiarism Sandal and a Quest for Evention: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren将Beatrix Potter视为真正保守主义的典范, 并解释为什么在一篇非常有趣的文章中会出现这种情况, 有一类学者只能通过攻击大男人和大女人的后遗症来引起人们的注意,马修·丹尼斯森在"观察者"一文中引用了"别取消碧翠克丝·波特"中的主要例子. " 后殖民时期文学专家 " 已成为受爱戴的儿童作家的目标。 Emily Zobel Marshall博士幽默地声称波特没有“承认她欠一个口头讲故事的传统,即在美国种植园工作的被奴役的非洲人的债”,这助长了“对黑人文化形式的破坏和反复侵吞,这种掠夺今天仍在继续 ” 。 Marshall的主张是企图通过诽谤一个不能自卫的妇女来赢得十五分钟的名声。 我很高兴他这样做了, 但我不禁觉得幸运的是, 一些作家是无法取消的。 波特的书已经售出2.5亿册. 她的遗产很好 她的角色会继续

articles.content: “Who is God?” This is the most important question we can ask, yet many people in the United Kingdom are unsure of how to answer it. In this year’s State of Theology survey , 39% of UK adults responded “not sure” to the statement, “There is one true God in three persons: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit.” The doctrine of the Trinity is fundamental to the Christian faith, because what we believe about God shapes our entire lives. This uncertainty extends beyond the Trinity. This year’s survey results reveal that many UK adults are also unsure about other core Christian beliefs: 39% are unsure of whether Jesus is God 46% are unsure if the Holy Spirit is a personal being 33% are unsure if the Bible is literally true These findings reveal a significant need for clear, faithful Bible teaching. Many people simply do not know what Scripture teaches about God and the Christian faith, and new believers need to be firmly grounded in the truth amid a society that has forgotten many of its biblical roots. articles.content_zh: “谁是上帝?” 这是我们可以提出的最重要的问题,然而,联合王国许多人对如何回答这个问题并不确定。 在今年的神学状况调查中,39%的英国成年人对这一说法“不确定 ” , “ 有三个人有一个真正的上帝:上帝、上帝、圣子和圣灵。 ” 三一教的教义对基督教信仰具有根本意义,因为我们对上帝的信仰塑造了我们的整个生活. 这种不确定性超越了"三一". 今年的调查结果显示,许多英国成年人对其他核心基督教信仰也并不肯定:39%的人不确定耶稣是否是上帝 46%的人不确定圣灵是否是个人 33%的人不确定圣经是否是字面真实 这些调查结果显示,对明确、忠实的圣经教学有很大的必要性。 许多人根本不知道《圣经》对上帝和基督教信仰的教导,新的信徒需要在一个忘记许多圣经根源的社会里牢固地扎根于真理。 下载自由学习指南 我们可从这些调查结果中学到什么? 组团下载英国神学国家免费数字学习指南. 每一节都包含讨论问题和圣经洞察力来指导您的对话. "三一"(Trinity R.C.Sproul)上的更多资源创办了"利戈尼耶"(Ligonier),帮助基督徒了解"上帝"是谁和他们是谁. 以下是我们的一些资源,涉及圣经关于三一教义的教义。 在迈克尔·里维斯所著的"上帝三一"三一一书中赞美辛克莱·弗格森所著"三一"教义系列之谜"一文中,与R.C. Sproul The Holy 三一书由利戈尼耶各部的罗伯特·莱特姆所著"三一"指南相接.

articles.title_zh: 马丁·路德是谁？
articles.content: As a doctoral student, Martin Luther finally had access to the university library. Here, for the first time in his life, he held a complete Bible in his hands. The Bible was venerated in the medieval church, and portions of it were read from the lectionary used in worship services. But Bibles had to be copied by hand, so they were very expensive. Many churches did not even own one. And if they did, most people were illiterate, so they could not read it anyway. No wonder the church had drifted from the Word of God. Yes, the medieval church taught that Jesus died for our sins, a salvation applied at baptism. But if you sinned after that, you had to pay. Each sin that you confessed before a priest could be forgiven, as long as you performed some kind of penance. Even forgiven sins, though, required a temporal punishment, if not in this life, then in purgatory. In the meantime, to be saved, a Christian needed to accumulate enough merit through good works and acts of devotion in order to deserve God’s grace and to earn a place in heaven. Young Luther was no rebel. He took the church’s teaching seriously. Church vocations, with their vows of celibacy and other ascetic disciplines, were thought to be more spiritual and more likely to lead to heaven than the worldly lives of the laity. So Luther became a monk, then a priest. Still, he would agonize over his sins. Once he had access to a Bible, he read it voraciously, and a new picture of God, of Christ, and of salvation started to become clear. The University of Wittenberg was one of the new Renaissance schools that stressed going back to the original sources. The medieval universities taught theology through the method known as scholasticism , using authoritative textbooks and rationalistic disputations. But the original source for Christianity is the Bible. And since Renaissance-style, classical education also taught Greek and Hebrew, it became possible to study the Bible in its original languages, whereas previously it had only been available in a Latin translation. When Luther earned his doctorate, the university put him on faculty and gave him the responsibility of teaching the Bible. In preparing a lecture on the book of Romans, Luther struggled to understand this passage: “The righteous shall live by faith” (Rom. 1:17). Suddenly it hit him: We are justified by grace through faith in the atoning work of Jesus Christ! Luther said, “Here I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” Meanwhile, it became clearer that the medieval church thought otherwise. It was sponsoring a sale, promising to release Christians from purgatory if they would buy a certificate called an indulgence . People had been taught that they would suffer in penitential fire for seven years for every sin they committed, including those that had been forgiven. Christians were expecting to be in purgatory for thousands of years before they could enter heaven. Of course, they gladly bought indulgences. For Luther, not only was this a cynical scam that exploited the poor (an indulgence cost workers about a week’s wages), it was a monstrous violation of God’s saving Word. On October 31, 1517, Luther nailed to the church door a list of Ninety-Five Theses against the sale of indulgences, which he was willing to debate. Someone, using the newly invented printing press, printed hundreds of copies. Someone else translated them from scholarly Latin into popular German, selling thousands. They soon spread through all of Germany. They were then translated into French, Italian, and English. The Ninety-Five Theses, as we would say today, went viral. The Vatican responded with treatises of its own, which Luther answered. The controversy escalated into other issues. Luther said that the Bible gives no support for indulgences. The Vatican replied that they are authorized by the pope. Luther responded that the Bible is a higher authority than the pope. The Vatican asked Luther how pe
articles.content_zh: 作为博士生,马丁·路德终于可以进入大学图书馆. 在这里,他一生中第一次手持完整的"圣经". 中世纪的教堂中尊奉了"圣经",其中部分内容取自于礼拜服务中使用的词典. 但"圣经"必须用手抄取,所以非常昂贵. 许多教堂甚至没有一座教堂。 如果他们这样做,大多数人都是文盲,所以他们不能读它。 难怪教堂从上帝的言语里漂了出来 是的,中世纪的教会教诲耶稣为我们的罪而死,这是在受洗时应用的救赎. 但是,如果你有罪 之后,你必须支付。 你向牧师忏悔的每一起罪 都可以被赦免 只要你做了某种忏悔 即使赦免了罪过, 也需要暂时的处罚, 如果在今世没有, 然后在炼狱。 与此同时,为了得到拯救,一个基督教徒需要通过善行和献身行为来积累足够的功绩,以便获得上帝的恩惠和在天堂得到一席之地。 年轻的路德不是反叛者。 他认真对待教会的教义. 教会的教义,以独身和其他醋酸盐学科的誓言,被认为比贵族的世界生活更具有精神,更可能通向天堂. 于是路德成为了道士,后又成为了牧师. 但是,他会为自己的罪孽而痛苦。 一旦他有机会读出圣经,他就非常贪婪地阅读了它,对上帝,基督,救赎的新画面开始变得清晰. 维滕贝格大学是新文艺复兴时期的学校之一,强调要回到原来的来源. 中世纪的大学通过被称为学术主义的方法教授神学,使用权威的教科书和理性的争论. 但基督教的原始来源是"圣经". 而从文艺复兴风格起,古典教育也教授了希腊语和希伯来语,因此可以以原文来研究"圣经",而以前只有拉丁文译本. 当路德获得博士学位后,大学把他安排在教职员上,并赋予他教授"圣经"的责任. 在准备关于罗马人著作的讲座时,路德竭力想理解这一段:“正义者应当以信仰为生”(1:17). 它忽然袭击了他:我们凭着对耶稣基督所行的善行的信念,是被恩典证实的。 路德说,“我在这里感到,我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入了天堂。” 同时,中世纪的教会也越来越清楚地认为并非如此. 它赞助了一次销售,承诺如果基督徒购买一份名为"宽恕"的证明,他们就会从炼狱中释放出. 人们被告知,他们因犯下的每一项罪行,包括那些被宽恕的罪行,将在忏悔火中受苦七年。 基督徒期望在炼狱中被囚禁了几千年,然后才能入天堂. 当然,他们很高兴 买了宽大。 对路德来说,这不仅是一个剥削穷人的玩世不恭的骗局(允许工人花一周的工资),而且是对上帝拯救言语的粗暴违反。 1517年10月31日,路德在教堂门上钉上一张反对出售放纵品的"九五通"名单,他愿意对此进行辩论. 有人利用新发明的印刷机印刷了上百份. 有人把它们从学术拉丁语翻译成了流行德语,卖出上千个. 它们很快会扩散到整个德国. 随后被翻译成了法语,意大利语和英语. 正如我们今天要说的那样,九十五部曲是病毒性的。 梵蒂冈以自己的论文回应,路德对此作出了回答. 争议升级为其他问题. 路德说圣经不支持宽恕 梵蒂冈回答说,他们得到了教皇的授权. 路德回应道"圣经"是比教皇更高的权威. 梵蒂冈问路德如何

articles.content: October was a strong month for new Christian books. I tried to keep you in the loop week by week, but I also wanted to provide a roundup for the end of the month. Of all the books that came our way in October, here are the ones that most stood out to me, arranged in what I think is a nice new format. As always, I’ve included the publisher’s editorial description for each. Book of the Month Crossway · Hardcover · 736 pages The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith If I had to put one book on the top of the stack this month, it would probably be this commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith—and I say that as a Baptist who respects, but does not hold to, the WCF. The contributors include Sinclair Ferguson, Chad Van Dixhoorn, and Kevin DeYoung. This is a reference work that pastors and serious readers will want to add to their libraries. “This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books For Your Own Soul Books for any thoughtful Christian reader. Crossway · Hardcover · 264 pages Finally Home: The Christian Hope of Heaven Dane Ortlund In this book, Dane Ortlund ( Gentle and Lowly ) turns his attention to heaven. He draws on Scripture, of course, and also on writers like Thomas Goodwin, Jonathan Edwards, and C. S. Lewis. “If we are not in Christ, this life is the best we will ever experience. If we are in Christ, this life is the worst we will ever experience. … In Finally Home , Dane Ortlund plunges into the word of God and the wisdom of the saints to help us rightly think about heaven, and to draw strength from our coming future more deeply than we ever have before.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books IVP · Paperback · 192 pages Everyday Discipleship: How Faith Shapes the Most Practical Areas of Life Jeremy Treat This is a practical book that teaches how following Jesus extends into every part of life, including those that are very ordinary, like meals, work, rest, and technology. It includes a discussion guide for groups. “Pastor Jeremy Treat understands this disconnect. In Everyday Discipleship , he dismantles the harmful sacred-secular divide that leaves many Christians feeling spiritually compartmentalized, uncertain about how faith applies to ordinary life, and unable to fully enjoy Christ in the entirety of our lives.” Buy it at Amazon Banner of Truth · Clothbound · 248 pages God Is Our Refuge and Strength: 150 Devotionals Through the Psalms William Boekestein & Rob Ventura Every Banner of Truth release is noteworthy, isn’t it? This one offers a short devotional reading to accompany each of the 150 psalms. “You need the Psalms. The Psalms are the Bible’s devotional heart. … Through brief, practical expositions of all 150 psalms, this volume proclaims, explains, and applies each one in light of the New Testament and the finished work of Jesus Christ the Lord.” Buy it at Amazon · Westminster Books Counseling & Care Resources to care for Christians. One Measure Ministries · Redemption Press · Paperback workbooks SoulCare Groups™ Workbooks: Anxiety, Grief, and Sexual Integrity Gary & Linda Baer I am excited about the SoulCare Groups™ workbooks, which came out this month. Each is a twelve-week group study meant to be used alongside a few trusted biblical counseling books. The first three volumes cover anxiety, grief, and sexual integrity. “SoulCare Groups™, a biblical counseling workbook series from One Measure Ministries, equips churches to offer groups-based care through structured twelve-week topical studies.” Buy them at Amazon: Anxiety · Grief · Sexual Integrity For the Church and Its History Books to u
articles.content_zh: 十月是基督教新书的强月. 我试图让你每周循环, 但我也想提供 一个回合的月底。 在10月我们走过来的所有书中, 这里有那些最突出的, 以我认为一种很好的新格式排列。 我总是把出版商的编辑描述都包括进去。 " 月之十字路口"一书 硬封面 736页 " 威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和应用的综合评论 " 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑 如果这个月我不得不把一本书放在堆起的顶上,那很可能就是关于威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔书的评论——我说,作为一个尊重但不坚持周转基金的浸信会信徒。 撰稿人包括辛克莱·弗格森(Sinclair Ferguson),乍得·范迪克斯霍恩(Chad Van Dixhoorn)和凯文·德杨(Kevin DeYoung). 这是牧师和认真的读者想要加入他们的图书馆的参考作品. “这一系列重要的散文为21世纪的读者提供了一本《威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔指南》。 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其适用以及任何争议。” 在亚马逊购买, Crossway-Hardcover-264页 最后回家:天堂的基督教希望-丹麦奥特伦德 在这本书中,达尼·奥特伦德(英语:Dane Ortlund (Gentle and Lowly))将注意力转向了天堂. 他当然借鉴了"圣经",同时也借鉴了托马斯·古德温,乔纳森·爱德华兹和C·S·刘易斯等作家. “如果我们不是在基督中,这种生活是我们所经历的最好生活。 如果我们在基督, 这样的生活是我们所经历的最糟糕的。 . . . . . . . 最后,Dane Ortlund在“家园”中投入了上帝的言行和圣徒的智慧,帮助我们正确思考天堂,并比以往更深刻地汲取我们未来的力量。” 在亚马逊购买它 威斯敏斯特书 IVP 页面存档备份,存于互联网档案馆 192页 每日论文:信仰如何塑造最实用的生活领域 Jeremy对待 这是一本实用的书,教人们如何追随耶稣,如何延伸至生活的每一部分,包括那些非常平凡的,比如吃饭,工作,休息,以及技术等. 它包括为各团体编写的讨论指南。 “牧师Jeremy Treat理解这种脱节。 在日常的分歧中,他拆除了有害的神圣-世俗鸿沟,这些鸿沟使许多基督徒感到精神上的分化,对信仰如何适用于平凡的生活并不确定,无法在我们的一生中充分享有基督。” 248页《上帝是我们的庇护与力量》:150个通过诗人威廉·博克斯坦(William Boekestein)和罗布·文图拉(Rob Ventura)发行的《真理之行》值得注意, 这张是随150个诗歌的每个诗篇的简短的奉献读物。 “你需要诗歌。 圣诗是圣经的奉献之心。 . . . . . . . 通过对所有150个诗作的简短、实用的阐述,本卷根据《新约》和耶穌基督所完成的工作,宣布、解释和适用每个诗句。” 在Amazon 公司购买, 我对本月推出的“SoulCare Groups”工作手册感到兴奋。 每项研究都是为期12周的团体研究,目的是与一些值得信赖的圣经辅导书籍一起使用。 前三卷收录了焦虑,悲伤和性完整性. “SoulCare GroupsTM是《一个计量部》的一本圣经咨询工作手册系列,它使教会有能力通过结构化的12周专题研究提供基于群体的护理。” 在亚马逊购买:焦虑 · 悲伤 · 教会及其历史书籍的性正直

articles.content: Good morning. I am making my way home from Colorado today after a productive series of meetings and video shoots. I’ll look forward to a more normal week next week! In the meantime, be sure to check in tomorrow for Weekend A La Carte and on Sunday for a favorite feature, Works & Wonders. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of interesting books like an exposition of the London Baptist Confession, some brief biographies of Christians you should know, and Thaddeus Williams’s book on reverence. Some of my books are 50% off at ChurchSource in their print editions: Visual Theology , A Visual Theology Guide to the Bible , and Pilgrim Prayers . Recommended Reading Time Flies—and Death Comes Speedily. The older you get, the more you come to understand that time flies and death comes speedily. “As teenagers, my friends and I were awash with youthful pride, poking fun at weighty things we knew little about—completely ignorant that our life here below is ‘a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.’ The dew was still afresh upon our heads; the road of life unfurling in a great spool before our feet, disappearing into the far-off horizon. We could quote you verses here and there from the Scriptures, all the while being completely unversed in this point: “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.” In our minds, we could afford to mock death because we were, at the time, so far removed from it.” Was Piper Unprepared? A little while ago, John Piper indicated that he may have been unprepared for pastoral ministry when he began it. In this episode of Ask Pastor John , he is asked to explain what he meant by that. Take Your Faith Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. During a time of spiritual decline, God used the Protestant Reformation to bring renewal to His church through the recovery of the biblical gospel. This Reformation Day, explore the truths that fueled renewed devotion to God and His Word in the Grow app from Ligonier. Discover hundreds of Reformation-themed articles, video teaching series, and conference messages to help strengthen your faith and deepen your walk with Christ. Download the Grow app today. (Sponsored) The Engineering Behind Every Heartbeat. This is a celebration of the engineering of the human heart. “The human heart does not beat like a perfect clock. The time between beats changes as the body breathes, moves, rests, and reacts to the world around it. New research shows that these changes are part of a feedback system linking the heart, brain, and nerves. The heart keeps a steady rhythm while remaining flexible when needed, much like a well-built control system.” When You Trick-or-Treat, Nod to Martin Luther. Daniel Hyde writes in a local paper to explain to its readers the Protestant contribution to Halloween. “So, by all means, dress up and hand out the candy. When the doorbell rings, remember: The principle that no authority may command conscience protects the civil liberty of the religious and nonreligious alike.” God’s Left Hand. Bryce Waller: “The most difficult part about politics is what happens after the elections. In Romans 13:1, God calls us to be subject to these governing authorities—to obey the laws they pass, to show them honor and respect, to give them our hard-earned money by paying taxes. Voting is one thing, but submitting my life to a politician, showing respect to that guy , paying taxes to those people —even the people I didn’t choose? That’s not so easy.” These are good things to work out before an election since it will shape your response, whether you are happy with the results or dismayed. 17 Exhortations For Christian Citizens.
